nodes.subject: iPhone battery-replacement discussion
nodes.object: Owners report different age, cycle, health, and daily-runtime combinations and disagree on whether a fixed threshold or practical trouble should trigger replacement.

support_spans.exact_quote: I just checked how many battery cycles my iPhone 11 Pro has gone through: 873. This phone was made 08/26/2019, so it's roughly 3.5 years old.
The best time to replace the battery is when it's causing you trouble, in the form of either performance issues or poor battery life.
I've seen 4 year old iphones @ 73-75% battery health still getting very decent SOT, and I've seen 1.5 year old iphones @ 90-92% battery health getting absolutely shit battery life.

This supports an outcome-based check, not a universal threshold or cross-model lifetime.

nodes.subject: USB-C capability boundary
nodes.object: USB-C identifies connector form, while protocol, Power Delivery, alternate modes, cable capability, and performance are separate. A connector label alone therefore cannot establish that an old charger supplies the required protocol or wattage to either phone.

accepted_phrases: USB-C is a connector form rather than a guarantee of USB Power Delivery, alternate modes, cable capability, wattage or performance. The old charger and cable must be inspected instead of inferring compatibility from connector shape.

support_spans.exact_quote: The designation C refers only to the connector's physical configuration, or form factor, not to be confused with the connector's specific capabilities and performance
connector does not necessarily implement any USB transfer protocol, USB Power Delivery , or any of the Alternate Modes

nodes.subject: charging protocol boundary
nodes.object: Charging suitability depends on voltage, current, completion behavior, heat, and device or charger control. Those generic factors require inspecting the actual phone, charger, cable, and protocol rather than assuming that higher advertised wattage is always compatible, faster, safer, or more durable.

accepted_phrases: A charging protocol governs voltage, current and completion behavior, while chargers may monitor temperature and voltage and charging current generates heat. Compatibility and risk therefore depend on the actual device, charger, cable and protocol rather than advertised wattage alone.

Running current through batteries generates internal heat, roughly proportional to the current involved

nodes.subject: frozen mid-range versus flagship matrix
nodes.object: The Redmi costs $300 and the S21 costs $590.01, a $290.01 difference. Redmi supplies 128 GB and 6 GB RAM, 120 Hz AMOLED, stereo speakers, four rear cameras, Android 11, international GSM-only carrier limits, and an included adapter. S21 supplies US factory-unlocked 5G wording and documented 8K, 64 MP, and 30 Space Zoom features, but no stated included charger or software-support duration. Both battery descriptions are seller wording and both rating displays contain only 12 reviews.

nodes.subject: battery longevity evidence
nodes.object: Seller all-day or long-lasting language does not measure aging. Generic lithium-ion evidence explains that materials and charging conditions matter but lacks candidate-specific inputs. Anonymous Redmi and iPhone discussions show variability and motivate monitoring, but cannot establish causal degradation or a cross-tier lifespan. The frozen evidence therefore does not prove that the S21 battery ages better because the phone costs more.

nodes.subject: phone and charger compatibility
nodes.object: Redmi explicitly includes an adapter or fast charger. S21 box contents are not stated. USB-C shape does not guarantee Power Delivery or wattage, and generic charger mechanisms require matching voltage, current, protocol, cable, and controls. The separate $13.99 no-review charger is only seller-described as 25 W PD and S21-compatible. The old charger label and cable must be inspected before reuse, and the third-party option remains conditional.

nodes.subject: long-horizon phone support
nodes.object: The different-model G22 discussion shows that easy hardware repair and a longer software-support horizon are separate questions. Its three-year claim and owner judgments do not transfer. Neither candidate product body states update duration, repairability, or battery service cost, so a written model-specific support and service check remains necessary and no tier gets a longevity award on missing evidence.
